name: Alicante
coordsNote: City centre (Explanada / Rambla); Playa de San Juan is ~7 km north-east by TRAM.

english.rationale: Spain is in the EF EPI Moderate band (score 540) -> tier 1, same as Valencia and Málaga. Northern-European residents are concentrated in the coastal towns around the city (and Playa de San Juan) rather than the centre, so no expat-hub bump.

sources.title: EF EPI — Spain
sources.note: Spain EF EPI score 540, rank #36 (Moderate band, 500-549).

vibe: Palm-lined port city, castle-topped hill, dry mild winters, Costa Blanca by tram
narrative: A working Spanish port city with the beach in town: the palm-lined Explanada, Santa Bárbara castle on Mount Benacantil, El Postiguet below the old town and the long Playa de San Juan a tram ride away, with rice dishes and an old-town tapas quarter (El Barrio). Winters are dry and mild and rents run about 15% under Valencia's and Málaga's, but July–August is hot and humid.

season.rationale: Editorial estimate. July–August is the beach peak. Winter is no longer dead: city hotel occupancy hit a record 59.3% in January and 80% (90% at Playa de San Juan) in February 2026, driven by northern-European winter visitors; Hogueras fills June and the Santa Faz pilgrimage April. Nov, Dec and Jan are the relative lulls.

events.name: Hogueras de San Juan (Fogueres)
events.blurb: weeks of mascletàs and parades, the bonfire monuments burned on the night of 24 June after a firework palm from Mount Benacantil, then a beach fireworks contest 25–29 June

source.title: Alicante Turismo — The Bonfires of Saint John 2026. Programme
source.note: 2026: festival 4–24 June, plantà 19–20 June, cremà night 24 June, International Fireworks Competition 25–29 June at Postiguet.

events.name: Romería de la Santa Faz
events.blurb: around 330,000 pilgrims walk the ~6 km from the old town to the Santa Faz monastery on the second Thursday after Easter

source.title: Ayuntamiento de Alicante — Unos 330.000 peregrinos ponen sus miradas en la Santa Faz (16 Apr 2026)
source.quote: Unos 330.000 peregrinos han dirigido este jueves su mirada hacia la Santa Faz

safety.propertyNote: Beach and old-town petty theft; calm overall

rationale.property: Editorial estimate. FCDO's Spain advice (distraction theft, airport/luggage theft, highway pirates targeting hire cars) applies; nothing Alicante-specific. A mid-size coastal city comparable to Valencia and Málaga, so set at their 70.
rationale.tourist: No sign visitors are targeted beyond normal pickpocketing; 1.0 like Valencia and Málaga.
rationale.womens: No women-specific concerns beyond the national pattern; kept at the Spain Gallup baseline like Valencia and Málaga.

consulted.title: UK FCDO — Spain: safety and security
consulted.quote: Be alert to the risk of street crime. Thieves use distraction techniques and often work in teams.

consulted.title: Travel Pirates — US Spain travel advisory Level 2 (Ceuta raised to Level 3)
consulted.note: Secondary report of the 1 Aug 2026 State Department update: Spain Level 2 (terrorism, unrest); only Ceuta is Level 3.

consulted.title: U.S. State Department travel advisories RSS feed (official)

selection: Costa Blanca's long-stay hub for northern-European retirees and remote workers: mild dry winters, rents ~15% below Valencia and Málaga (idealista, Sep 2026).
researchNotes: US advisory: travel.state.gov returned HTTP 403 / a Cloudflare bot check, so the advisory page itself could NOT be opened. Level 2, date 2026-08-01 and risks (Terrorism, Unrest) come from a web-search snippet of the State Dept page plus the Travel Pirates write-up; the catalog currently shows Spain dated 2026-06-09 (Málaga) and 2025-05-12 (Valencia) — reconcile centrally. Not flagged as a hazard: autumn DANA cloudbursts (Sept–Oct) cause occasional flash floods on this coast; Valencia carries no such flag either. Semana Santa omitted because I did not verify a source this session.
